title: Advisory Locks for Distributed Idempotency and Rate Limiting
realWorldScenario: An e-commerce API allows customers to redeem a single-use coupon code. High-concurrency automated scripts send 20 requests within 50 milliseconds using the same coupon code. Multiple requests succeed simultaneously before the `used` flag can be checked and written.
questionStatement: Design a concurrency-safe single-use coupon redemption mechanism using PostgreSQL advisory locks. Contrast using `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(coupon_code))` against `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`, explaining deadlocks, memory consumption, and transaction isolation interactions.
expectedConcepts: Serialization of concurrent requests for identical resource
Advantages over row-level locks when rows do not yet exist (insert race)
Zero disk I/O and zero tuple bloat in shared memory lock table
hints: What happens if the row does not exist yet? Can SELECT FOR UPDATE lock a non-existent row?
hashtext() converts a string to a 32-bit integer for the lock key.
Transaction-level advisory locks release automatically on COMMIT.
